records.quote:
The first shot tore squarely through his heart. And while he stood
staring at her, mouth agape, a second shot burned its way through his
bewildered brain.
records.paraphrase: The girl shoots Hyrel's projected self twice, in the heart and brain.

records.quote:
The telovis, of a stereoscopic nature,
seemingly brought the performers with all their tinsel and color
directly into the room of the watcher.
records.paraphrase: A device called the telovis projects three-dimensional images of performers into the viewer's room.

records.quote:
It was comforting to know that
it was there, exhilarating to know that he could escape for a few hours
by a mere flick of his finger.
records.paraphrase: Hyrel feels exhilaration at the ability to escape via the telporter switch.

records.quote:
Strange how a device such as the
telporter suit could cause the shadow of each bodily cell to leave the
body, materialize, and become a reality in its own right.
records.paraphrase: The telporter suit is said to make the shadow of each bodily cell leave the body and materialize as a separate reality.

records.quote:
the pain of the cut had remained in his hand, but there was
no sign of the cut itself on the hand of his outer self. The scar was
peculiar to the shadowy body only. There was something about the shadowy
body that carried the hurts to the outer body, but not the scars....
records.paraphrase: Injuries to the shadow body transfer pain but not visible scars to the outer body, explained as a property of the telportation.

records.quote:
This she folded neatly and tucked
away into the false back of the medicine cabinet.
records.paraphrase: The wife hides her own telporter suit, revealing she had used the same technology to trap and kill him.

records.quote:
She stood a moment longer, watching his eyes become glazed and
sightless. Then she walked to the telephone.
records.paraphrase: The wife calmly watches her husband die before calling the police.

records.quote:
something
within him--his ectoplasm, higher self, the thing spirits use for
materialization, whatever its real name--streamed out of him along an
invisible channel, leaving his body behind in the chair in a conscious
but dream-like state. His other self materialized in a small cabin
records.paraphrase: The suit causes an inner self to stream out of the body along an invisible channel and materialize elsewhere while the body remains behind.

records.quote:
You pressed a tiny switch on the
telporter suit; you were whisked away to a receiving set you had
previously set up in secret.
records.paraphrase: The telporter suit, activated by a switch, transports the user to a pre-set receiving location.

records.quote:
It catered to a clientele that had but three
things in common: money, a desire for utter self-abandonment, and a
sales slip indicating ownership of a telporter suit. The club was of
necessity expensive, for self-telportation was strictly illegal, and
police protection came high.
records.paraphrase: In this world self-telportation is illegal, and an exclusive club serves owners of telporter suits under police protection.

records.quote:
His other self materialized in a small cabin in a
hidden nook between a highway and a river where he had installed the
receiving set a month ago.
records.paraphrase: His projected self appears at a distant cabin where he installed a receiver.

records.quote:
There upon the bed now reposed her shell of reality while her inner
self, the shadowy one, completely materialized, became an exotic thing
from the East in this never-never land.
records.paraphrase: Club patrons leave their bodies at home while their materialized inner selves indulge in escapist personas.

records.quote:
He looked at the heel of his left hand. There was a long, irregular scar
there. It was the result of a cut he had received nearly three weeks ago
records.paraphrase: Hyrel examines a scar on his shadow body to work out how injuries transfer between the two selves.

records.quote:
Then she bent over him and reached down
his thigh until her fingers contacted the small switch.
records.paraphrase: His wife, who was the disguised girl, presses his switch to recall his fatally shot shadow self to his body.

records.quote:
Seconds later, a slight tremor shook Hyrel's body. His eyes snapped
open, air escaped his lungs, his lower jaw sagged inanely, and his head
lolled to one side.
records.paraphrase: When his shadow self returns, Hyrel's body dies from the injuries carried back.

records.quote:
the shadowy
self got drunk and had a good time, and the outer husk suffered the
hangover in the morning.
records.paraphrase: The narrative contrasts the projected self's experiences against the consequences felt by the original body.

criteria.rationale: The story offers a pseudo-scientific rationalization of the telporter effect (ectoplasm, cellular shadows materializing), but the treatment is explicitly spiritualist/hand-waved rather than a materially represented scientific fact, theory, or natural process. The plausible science-adjacent reading is present but interpretively uncertain.

The telporter suit is an engineered invention that drives the setting, the protagonist's escapes, the club subculture, and the entire murder mechanism. The injury-transfer property of the device is the direct cause of the fatal outcome, making the technology central to problem, action, and resolution.

The telportation is spatial projection of a shadow-self, not temporal displacement, and the setting is a near-contemporary society rather than a speculative future or remote past. No material instance of future/remote past/time travel is present.

The whole plot extrapolates consequences from the telporter premise: an illegal escapist subculture, and crucially the rule that injuries to the shadow self transfer as fatal harm to the body. The wife weaponizes this established property by shooting the projected self and recalling it to kill him, a consequence developed directly from the technological premise.

Hyrel examines the scar and reasons out the rule that the shadow body carries hurts but not scars to the outer body, a moment of observation and inference about the device's behavior. However, it is a brief reflective deduction, not a sustained systematic method driving action, so materiality is uncertain.

All locations are ordinary terrestrial settings (home, a riverside club, a cabin). The 'never-never land' is metaphorical escapism, not another planet, dimension, or nonordinary cosmic environment, and there are no visitors from such places.

The events are an individual murder via the telporter mechanism, a personal death rather than a natural, technological, cosmic, biological, or human-caused large-scale disaster. There is no catastrophe of broader scale that is actual, impending, remembered, or causally central.

candidates.description: The telporter suit, a device that causes the user's inner/shadow self (each bodily cell's shadow) to detach and materialize as a distinct, autonomous reality at a remote receiver, while the original body remains behind in a dreamlike state. Injuries incurred by the shadow self transfer as pain and lethal harm to the body but not visible scars, and pressing the switch recalls the shadow self.

novelty.rationale: The telporter suit constitutes a totalizing difference from the empirical norm: a technology that splits selves into body and materialized shadow, restructuring social life (illegal escapist clubs, private-room culture, police protection) around this bifurcated existence. This is a world-altering premise, not an incidental gadget.

cognitive_validation.rationale: The story presents the device with an internally consistent, systematic, immanent logic analogized to radio/TV/telovis transmission (impulse or wave carrying something from body to a receiver). It has stable rules: body remains conscious-dreamlike, shadow materializes at a pre-set receiver, injuries carry pain but not scars, the switch recalls the self. Hyrel even reasons empirically about the scar/pain transfer. The language of 'ectoplasm, higher self, the thing spirits use' gestures toward the spiritual, creating mild ambiguity, but the framing is consistently technological and rule-governed rather than genuinely supernatural, satisfying imaginary-science coherence.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The entire plot logic depends on the telporter suit: Hyrel's double life and alibi ambitions, the club setting, and crucially the murder mechanism. The wife exploits the injury-transfer rule and the recall switch to kill him by shooting his shadow self and returning it to his body. The novum determines the overriding narrative outcome; without it the story cannot exist.

estrangement.rationale: The narrative contrasts the shadow self's revels against the outer body's suffering (the drunk shadow, hangover body), and dramatizes the storyworld transformation via an illegal escapist club and the wife's lethal exploitation of the recall/injury-transfer mechanics.

candidates.description: The telovis, a personalized stereoscopic three-dimensional broadcast device worn on the head that projects performers with full color and emotional coloring directly into the viewer's room, used here for immersive black-market sex-operas.

novelty.rationale: The telovis is a novel media technology beyond the empirical norm, delivering emotion-colored 3D immersive broadcasts, an extrapolation of television.

cognitive_validation.rationale: It is described in coherent, nonsupernatural terms as a stereoscopic broadcast device carrying images by electrical impulse or wave, consistent with the story's media technology.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The telovis is an incidental device: it merely keeps the wife occupied and provides a cover for her own telportation. It does not govern the narrative logic; that role belongs to the telporter suit. It is a supporting prop, not the dominant novum.

estrangement.rationale: The telovis estranges by presenting immersive personalized broadcast entertainment as ordinary domestic furniture, but it drives no story-level transformation.
